title: Finite refinements and local lifting
statement:
For a quasi-compact quasi-separated $X$, split etale hypercovers finite in
each degree [def-weil-pbc-finite-split-hypercover] exist. Their homotopy
category is cofiltered. A finite collection of local lifting requirements on
their terms in finitely many degrees can be satisfied after refinement,
provided each requirement is locally solvable for the etale topology.
Consequently an arbitrary etale hypercover can, through any specified finite
degree, be refined by one finite in each degree.

proof.text: Existence follows from the finite split existence construction. A finite split hypercover has the ordinary hypercover condition by its stored matching witnesses. The product of two such hypercovers is a hypercover. Its all-degree finite split replacement maps to both factors by composition with the product projections. For parallel maps take the ordinary endpoint-path homotopy equalizer hypercover, replace it by a finite split one, and precompose its elementary homotopy; this gives an EqvGen relation.

source.place: Lemmas 01GI (lemma-product-hypercoverings) and 01GS (lemma-homotopy), proof with the endpoint mapping object, using Lemma 01GN (lemma-add-simplices); Lemma 094K for the finite split replacement

proof.text: For finitely many prescribed locally solvable lifts in degrees at most $r$, list in advance their pullbacks along every degeneracy from a lower degree at most $r$; there are finitely many such maps in each bounded degree. When constructing a nondegenerate component in degree $m$, impose all requirements on it, including these pullbacks of requirements from higher degrees, before fixing that degree. Local solvability supplies finitely many etale covering families. Cover the quasi-compact matching component by finitely many affine opens using [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-finite-affine-open-cover], pull back the local-lifting covers to them by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], and take a common finite affine refinement of the resulting finite family with [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-affine-refinement]. That choice defines $N_m$ and its lifts at once; every degree-$n$ degenerate copy, $n\leq r$, inherits its required lift from its lower nondegenerate source. Repeat through $r$ and use the unconstrained extension of step 2 above $r$.

source.place: Lemma 01GK (lemma-covering-sheaf), proof, and Lemma 01GJ (lemma-covering), construction of a refinement lifting local data in a chosen degree; Lemma 094K for finite covers

proof.text: Let $K$ be any etale hypercover and fix $r$. Build a split $V$ and a map $V\to K$ by the same induction. If the map is already defined below $n$, the relative target for the new summand is $M_n(V)\times_{M_n(K)}K_n$. Its projection to $M_n(V)$ is the base change of the covering $K_n\to M_n(K)$ and hence is a covering by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]. The matching components of $M_n(V)$ are quasi-compact by step 1, so that step gives finite affine refinements of the relative cover over them for $n\leq r$, without requiring the terms of $K$ themselves to be quasi-compact. The chosen maps into the relative target define both the new faces and the map $V_n\to K_n$. Above $r$ continue with the ordinary finite split extension from step 2, carrying along the relative target if a full refinement of $K$ is required. This yields the stated finite split refinement through $r$, and an all-degree finite split refinement when the induction is continued.

source.place: Lemma 01GJ (lemma-covering), statement and relative-cover construction; Lemma 0DAV, split extension; Lemma 094K, finiteness of each degree
